subject: CirrusPay — inference economics recap & pilot budget check
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Kline <jordan@cirruspay.com>, Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@cirruspay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: CirrusPay — inference economics recap & pilot budget check

Thanks for the convo today — quick recap and proposed next steps to align around budget and pilot scope. High-level goal: validate a production path for mailbox classification + smart suggestions with predictable unit economics and <1x latency impact vs baseline.

What we heard (pain & goals)
- Current: in-house model latency spikes at peak (avg 220ms tailing to 800ms), topline token spend is unpredictable because of fanout to multiple models.
- Goal: bring inference unit cost down ~35% while keeping P95 latency under 400ms, and enable a safe pilot with production-like traffic.

Primary levers we discussed
- Model variant: 13B quantized variant (post-op kernels) for most requests; fall back to 70B dense for edge cases.
- Batching: target effective batch size 6-10 for your QPS shape — reduces per-token GPU overhead.
- KV/prefix caching: reuse conversational context across similar requests — expect ~20–30% token reduction for classification flows.
- Token trimming & output constraints: short structured responses for suggestions to cut generative token volume.

Preliminary TCO framing (rough order of magnitude)
- Pilot A (conservative): 2x A100-equivalent reserved instances, quantized 13B, expected net token cost ~$6k/mo (model + infra) + $2k/mo platform = ~$8k/mo.
- Pilot B (aggressive): 1x reserved + burst, aggressive caching & batching, expected net token cost ~$3.5k/mo + $1.5k/mo platform = ~$5k/mo.
Note: these are starting points — final pricing depends on 30-day usage profile and target SLOs.

Attachments: RWI_CirrusPay_TCO_playbook_v1.pdf (playbook + sample calculations), request: please share a recent 30-day usage snapshot (tokens/day, peak QPS by minute) — I attached a CSV template (cirruspay_usage_snapshot_aug2026.csv).

Asks / next steps
1) Jordan — can you confirm an acceptable monthly pilot budget range (ballpark) and any procurement timing constraints?
2) Share the 30-day usage snapshot or give us access to a raw export (tokens per minute preferred).
3) If budget looks feasible, we propose a 6-week pilot: weeks 0–1 onboard & baseline, weeks 2–4 tuning (batching/caching), week 5 smoke & metrics, week 6 handoff + scaling plan.

If it helps, we can produce two explicit SOW options (Pilot A/B above) with pricing and success criteria.

Thanks — happy to sync again tomorrow if needed.

—

Thanks Alex — great summary. Two quick clarifications:
- Budget constraint: we have an internal cap of ~$20k/month for pilots that touch payment data (governance reasons). That should cover infra + platform for a 6-week test but we need line items for procurement.
- Success metric: aim to reduce per-transaction inference cost to under $0.0006 (including platform fees) or achieve a 30% cost reduction vs current.

I'll pull the 30-day extract and send it by EOD tomorrow. Procurement timeline: they need an SOW + cost breakdown; Liam will copy procurement once we have numbers.

—Jordan

Jordan — thanks, that budget cap is helpful. Quick follow-up with concrete pilot options based on your goal (<= $0.0006/tx OR 30% cost reduction):

Pilot option 1 — Robust (safer SLOs)- 2 reserved nodes (A100 equiv) running quantized 13B + fallback to 70B for <5% of requests- Target batching 8, KV caching on classification paths- Estimated monthly cost: $12k infra + $3k platform = $15k/mo- Expected result: ~30–40% cost reduction, P95 ~300–380ms

Pilot option 2 — Lean (cost-first)- 1 reserved node + burst; stronger prefix caching and token trimming; accept SLO slack for <1% of requests- Estimated monthly cost: $6.5k infra + $1.5k platform = $8k/mo- Expected result: ~25–35% cost reduction, P95 ~360–450ms

Notes & tradeoffs- Caching: we respect freshness windows; for payment-sensitive flows we isolate cached keys to avoid cross-tenant leakage.- Batching: effective gains depend on request interarrival; your peak-minute QPS will determine achievable batch sizes.

Action items
- Jordan: send the 30-day tokens/min and peak-minute QPS export.
- CirrusPay procurement: we'll prepare two SOWs (Option 1/2) with explicit line items. Ben, can you own the procurement SOWs and timeline?
- Monica: propose a tech deep-dive next week to validate the required network path and RBAC for the pilot (VPC peering or Private Connect).

Referencing attached playbook for the math tables.
